answer.text: Making investment decisions for the fund
Matching products to investor profiles, explaining disclosures and risk factors, advising on product/risk/investor fit, and assisting transaction documentation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 268, 270, 276), AIF distributors match products to investor profiles, provide support and relationship management, explain disclosures and risk factors and product fit, advise on product and risk profile/investor fit, and assist with transaction paperwork — always keeping investor suitability paramount. The Trap: Investment decisions, fee-setting, and investee approvals are functions of the investment manager and the fund's governance bodies — not the distributor. Note: The distributor's role is investor-facing and suitability-driven; it does not extend into the fund's investment or pricing decisions.
